propositions: Four-pass code-review architecture (find, verify, decide, coach) suffers repeated criterion drift when severity, drop/block policy, remediation instructions, or discretionary decisions leak across phase boundaries.

A new project-owned criterion `project.review-phase-boundaries` must emit grounded findings only, carry no severity/confidence/suggested_fix, and enforce strict phase ownership guards to prevent Pass-1 assessment/policy/remediation leaks, Pass-2 discovery/decision/fix leaks, LLM discretion in Pass 3, and Pass-4 re-adjudication.

A balanced 12-case eval corpus (RP-F1..RP-F6 must fire, RP-N1..RP-N6 must not fire) calibrates the single-turn finder across all six boundary violations and legitimate refinements, requiring recall=1.0, false_accept=0.0, agreement=1.0, stability_min≥2/3, and kappa≥0.70 across three live runs.

Committed project assets must include prompt routing with exec:1-TURN and blocking_enabled:false, prompt front matter with execution_mode:single_turn and outputs:code_review_findings, balanced YAML eval corpus, strict test suite, and docs/llm-framework.md subsection explaining project ownership and advisory posture.

Live semantic calibration on anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6 must record model, timestamp, all 36 executions, and exact metrics, with proof that ticket_context diff is interpolated into the resolved system prompt.

Implementation must change only declared project-owned files (.rebar/, .gitignore exception, criterion tests, docs subsection) with zero changes to kernel, Pass-3/4 seams, or blocking behavior; landing requires LLM-Review+1, Verified+1, and reachability from origin/main.
